items.list_title: Beyond sovereignty: nationally led crisis response in East Africa
items.title: Beyond sovereignty: nationally led crisis response in East Africa
items.summary: This policy brief draws some common findings from the examples of Kenya and Somalia, including both barriers and areas of practical progress through sub-national authorities, civil society and social protection mechanisms. These common findings are then considered in the context of Uganda, South Sudan and Ethiopia, each undergoing unique transitions and with lessons for state authorities, civil society, donors and international organisations.

items.title: Poverty and public finance: a primer
items.summary: A primer on how poverty is defined, measured and reported and how fiscal policy shapes poverty outcomes.

items.title: What makes finance ministry officials tick
items.summary: A survey of 142 finance ministry officials across low- and middle-income countries reveals how they navigate competing budget demands, and who they believe really holds influence over spending decisions.

items.title: Does EU aid promote EU exports?
items.summary: A 20-year empirical study shows every €1 in EU development cooperation to Africa is associated with €6.80 in European goods and services exports. Discover how investing in partner-country development actively strengthens European competitiveness and trade.

items.title: Resourcing LGBTQI+ movements in the Global South and East to build inclusive civic space
items.summary: Drawing on research from Pakistan, Thailand and Argentina, this Briefing Paper by ODI Global, ALIGN and the Global Philanthropy Project, argues that investment in LGBTQI+ movements is an investment in a more inclusive civic space – and, ultimately, in democracy.

items.title: The Taliban’s madrassa system in Afghanistan: the threat to global peace and security
items.summary: The Taliban’s development of an ideologically driven madrassa education system could pose risks to global peace and security. This ODI Policy Brief warns global policymakers about the implications of this emerging system.

items.summary: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) experience higher levels of loss and damage from extreme weather in relation to their gross domestic product (GDP) than any other group of countries. And new data suggests that an increasingly high proportion of these losses can be directly attributed to climate change.

items.summary: New independent research finds Manufacturing Africa (MA) has mobilised £2.2bn in FDI and 150,000 jobs since 2019, accelerating and strengthening investment into African manufacturing. The study assesses MA’s additionality and highlights its catalytic role in driving structural transformation.

items.summary: ODI Global advises leaders on driving positive change. We turn bold ideas, evidence, and broad expertise into actionable strategies for a more resilient, just and equitable future.

items.list_title: Oppression, liberation and humanitarianism in Palestine, Myanmar and Sudan
items.title: Oppression, liberation and humanitarianism in Palestine, Myanmar and Sudan
items.summary: This paper examines how historical and contemporary settler colonialism, compounded by predatory capitalism, drive extreme violence and vast humanitarian needs in Palestine, Myanmar and Sudan. They are not accidental crises but manufactured and sustained by oppressive power systems and malicious actors.

items.list_title: ODI Europe Impact Report: Bridging Europe and the world in a fragmented era
items.title: ODI Europe Impact Report: Bridging Europe and the world in a fragmented era
items.summary: Europe's role in the world is being tested, renegotiated, and reshaped in real time. As geopolitical rivalry intensifies, economic security reshapes strategic choices, and multilateral cooperation grows more contested, the assumptions that once underpinned European policymaking no longer hold. Our new impact report sets out how ODI Europe has worked over the past year to help Europe and its partners navigate this more complex and interconnected global landscape.

items.list_title: The EU–Malawi partnership: outlook for EU development cooperation

items.list_title: Delivering an ecosystem approach to humanitarian action: proposals from the Advisory Panel on the Future of Humanitarian
items.title: Delivering an ecosystem approach to humanitarian action: proposals from the Advisory Panel on the Future of Humanitarian Action
authors: Advisory Panel on the Future of Humanitarian Action
items.summary: The Advisory Panel on the Future of Humanitarian Action proposes an ecosystem approach to the humanitarian system, which would entail bolstering the local systems that already serve people in need, while addressing the power imbalances in terms of funding, decision-making, risk and accountability.
